reuse.why: Builds on the existing recurConfigToRSchedule (daily weekend skip via byDayOfWeek) and getDateWithSkippedWeekend (holiday-aware move), and RSchedule's own exdates/exrules for daily holiday skips, instead of post-filtering at each consumer.

duplication.why: Holiday matching and the move rule live once in shared/schedules.ts; the only repetition is the rrules + getHolidayExdates + getHolidayExrules construction, repeated in parseRecurDate, getUpcomingDates and getDatesInRange rather than wrapped in one schedule-building helper.

placement.why: Recurrence and weekend/holiday rules sit in shared/schedules.ts beside recurConfigToRSchedule and getDateWithSkippedWeekend; the new handler is in server/schedules/app.ts next to getUpcomingDates.

scope.why: Changes are limited to schedule recurrence, the new handler, the type field, tests and release notes.

maintainability.why: Skipping is expressed in the recurrence itself so every consumer gets it, and moving is one helper; the triple exdate/exrule wiring and the extra frequency !== 'daily' guard only in getDatesInRange are small hazards.

bypasses_abstraction.where: All consumers go through recurConfigToRSchedule and getDateWithSkippedWeekend; schedule-template.ts is updated to pass holidays.

disguised_duplication.where: The repeated RSchedule construction is a verbatim repeat of three helper calls, not a reshaped copy of logic.

abstraction_drift.where: getDateWithSkippedWeekend gains a holidays parameter and recurConfigToRSchedule a daily + skipWeekend branch, both the genuine variations the steps ask for; getDatesInRange adds a redundant frequency !== 'daily' guard around the shared move but still calls it.
